introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b)your name must be Makumba and your address CES de Monkwo.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for the events of last week, with the imparfait for the circumstances and feelings (*j'étais furieux*). A past tense is needed because the essay tells what has happened.

**Model essay** (142 words)

La semaine dernière, je me suis fâché contre mon camarade de classe. Pendant la récréation, il a pris mon stylo sans me demander la permission et il l'a cassé. J'étais furieux et je lui ai crié des mots très méchants. Il ne s'est pas excusé, alors nous ne nous sommes plus parlé pendant deux jours.

Heureusement, notre professeur principal a remarqué notre silence. Il nous a appelés dans son bureau et il nous a écoutés patiemment. Il nous a expliqué que la colère ne résout rien. Mon camarade a reconnu son erreur et il m'a offert un stylo neuf. De mon côté, je lui ai demandé pardon pour mes paroles.

Depuis ce jour, nous sommes plus proches qu'avant. Je suis devenu plus patient et lui est devenu plus attentif. Nous partageons nos affaires, nous travaillons ensemble et nous évitons les disputes inutiles.

**Notes**

The essay covers the three parts of the topic: what happened (the pen taken and broken, the quarrel, two days of silence), how the problem was solved (the form teacher listened to both boys, the classmate admitted his mistake and gave a new pen, the writer apologised), and the attitude of both after the reconciliation (closer, more patient and more attentive, sharing and working together). The writer is a boy (*fâché*, *devenu*). In *nous ne nous sommes plus parlé* the participle does not agree, because *se parler* takes an indirect object.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All three bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Giving only the quarrel and forgetting how it was solved or what happened afterwards: the three parts of the topic must all be covered.
2. Mixing tenses without a reason (for example the présent for the events in the middle of a story told in the passé composé).
